packetText:
# Slide 4 — Short Is Not the Intervention

## Status

- current deck numbering: slide 4
- legacy source mapping: same as current
- decision state: OPEN

## Why this slide exists

- anchor the talk in learning science
- prevent the audience from reducing microlearning to "shorter slides"
- create a framework the rest of the deck can reference

## Locked slide thesis

Microlearning works when it applies learning science, not when it merely shortens content.

## Slide purpose brief

- top claim:
  the mechanism is design, not duration
- support claim:
  four pillars make the approach coherent
- non-goals:
  - do not over-explain each pillar with dense text
  - do not look like a consulting framework slide

## Figure job

- make four pillars instantly understandable
- create a memorable framework image
- keep enough elegance that it feels like a keynote slide, not a handout

## Locked copy

- header:
  `Short is not the intervention.`
- subheader:
  `Microlearning works when it applies learning science.`
- figure labels:
  - `Spaced repetition`
  - `Active recall`
  - `Cognitive load`
  - `Just-in-time relevance`

## Visual rules

- strong center of gravity
- clear four-part logic
- no generic quadrant with tiny text

## Existing useful source assets

- `inputs/microlearning_emergency_medicine_review.md`
- `inputs/saem_microlearning_talk_outline.md`

## Immediate next refinement

- generate a first framework concept
- compare a radial model versus a stacked pillar model
